corrections_to_earlier_records: PV2_0150 README and commands.sh said 'Batch 250 x 40 batches x 10 epochs = 100,000 exposures exactly'. The argument default is 256, not 250, with a partial final batch, and PairDataset feeds two views per sample. The exposure count (10 passes over 10,000 unique images) is right; the arithmetic as written was not. No PV2_0150 number changes.

PV2_0151's own first draft listed Slot Attention's CLEVR background rule as global_largest with a predicted foreground of 0.8510. A_bg_rules.json says the selected rule was border_largest and the predicted foreground 0.7047; 0.8510 is the global_largest figure quoted in sa_bg.py's docstring. Corrected before the first push of the Slot Attention rows. No metric value changes.

PV2_0149 and this record's first draft justified deprioritising Rotating Features and the complex autoencoders on the grounds that 'their published numbers are already directly comparable on Multi-dSprites'. Checked: those figures come from SynCx's comparison table (arXiv 2405.17283, recorded at BENCHMARK_PLAN.md:97), not from each model's own paper, and the official Rotating Features repo (loeweX/RotatingFeatures, commit 7a2f38f) supports 4Shapes, FoodSeg103 and Pascal VOC only, with zero mentions of dSprites or multi-object-datasets. Its 0.84 is a third-party reproduction that is not checkable from the authors' code without a new loader and training config. No measured value in any record changes.
limitations: seed 0 everywhere; the contract judges 3-seed means
Tetrominoes foreground_iou margin is +0.0345 and we have no seed spread for AKOrN (conv): treat that single cell as unsettled
no seed spread at all for ItrSA or AKOrN (conv)
ItrSA, AKOrN (attn) and Slot Attention are all far from their published numbers at this budget; AKOrN (conv) is not
mBO here is not comparable to published mBO: the truth fed to the models is the grid quantisation, not the true pixel mask
fixed320 is a reserved evaluation split, not an independent original-paper test split
next: a second seed for AKOrN (conv): it is the one baseline that is not budget-limited and it owns our narrowest margin (7 min)
our own CLEVR seeds 1 and 2 remain the expensive unapproved item

SynCx (agopal42/syncx, same author and the same data/eval structure) is the cheapest remaining baseline; its published Multi-dSprites 0.82 is one of only two figures above ours and it carries the same per-image oracle
Rotating Features is the other figure above ours (0.84, SynCx's reproduction); its official repo supports 4Shapes/FoodSeg103/Pascal only, so it needs a loader written before it can be run at all
